newsitem.title: USA: SBC forms Swiss telecom joint venture.
newsitem.headline: SBC forms Swiss telecom joint venture.

text.p: SBC Commmunications Inc. said Thursday it completed a deal to form Diax, a new Swiss telecom venture to compete against the Swiss national Telecom Postal, Telephone & Telegraph company.

SBC said its partner in the joint venture is made of Switzerland's six utilities, which together will own 60 percent of Diax. SBC, the telecommunications operating partner of the venture, will own the remaining 40 percent.
The ownership structure had not been disclosed in the previously announced deal.
Additional details, including the level of investment, managment structure, staffing and board representation, will annnouced at a press conference in June in Switzerland.
SBC, based in San Antonio, Texas, said the Diax venture bolsters its presence in Europe ahead of January 1988, when many markets will be opened up to competition, including Switzerland's.
An SBC spokesman said the structure of deal remains to be approved by the Swiss government's competition commission, a process expected to be completed next month.
Diax faces competition not only from Swiss Telecom, but also a consortium formed by Swiss Federal Railways SBB, the supermarket chain Migro and Union Bank of Switzerland that is known as Newtelco AG.
"Diax represents a great blend of expertise that will benefit Swiss consumers and businesses," Edward Whiteacre, SBC's chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.
"No one knows the Swiss marketplace better than our utility company partners, and SBC's capabilities and experience in developing telecommunications companies around the world is unsurpassed."

Diax will be a full-service telecommunications provider to residential and business customers. It is constructing an advanced digital fiber optic network that will provide all major Swiss cities with rapid, high-quality transmission links nationwide.
SBC said Diax will also bid on Swiss wireless licenses when they become available.
